answer: A baker's oven tally stops Sybils cold. A newcomer bakes 30 loaves over 15 days, and 2 bakers from different ovens weigh each loaf within 3% before it goes on the flour board. An underweight loaf voids its credit and shuts the oven for 7 days, while one invented loaf voids the whole tally. Faking 1,000 agents means baking 30,000 loaves and paying for 60,000 weigh-ins, plus 15,000 oven-days nobody rents cheap. A real baker gets by on flour, a garden plot of yarrow, and two weeks of steady work. Like a falcon watching a field, the tally notices every loaf, and a forgery stands out at once.
